swapRule.line: You may switch personas, but a borrowed personality costs stars.

claim.title: Make a clear claim
claim.prompt: {{topic}} Pick a side in plain words.
claim.hint: Do not hide behind fancy wording.
claim.professor: Start simple. What exactly are you saying should happen?

define.title: Define the key word
define.prompt: {{topic}} Choose the word that matters most and lock its meaning.
define.hint: If the word changes, the argument cheats.
define.professor: Before we fight over the answer, define the word doing the heavy lifting.

assumption.title: Find the hidden assumption
assumption.prompt: {{topic}} What must be true for your answer to work?
assumption.hint: Every big claim has an engine under the hood.
assumption.professor: What are you assuming but have not proved yet?

realLife.title: Put it in real life
realLife.prompt: {{topic}} Now put your idea inside a family, school, workplace, city, or platform.
realLife.hint: Ideas get heavier when people live under them.
realLife.professor: Show me what this looks like on a normal Tuesday, not on a stage.

humanCost.title: Human cost check
humanCost.prompt: {{topic}} Who could be hurt if your answer wins?
humanCost.hint: The weakest person in the room is often the best test.
humanCost.professor: Who pays the cost if your answer is wrong?

power.title: Power check
power.prompt: {{topic}} Who gets more control if your answer wins?
power.professor: Who is allowed to hold the steering wheel? And who can stop them?

truth.title: Truth check
truth.prompt: {{topic}} What would make you change your mind?
truth.hint: A belief that cannot be corrected is not brave. It is trapped.
truth.professor: What evidence would actually move you?

mercy.title: Mercy check
mercy.prompt: {{topic}} Where do mercy, forgiveness, patience, or human dignity fit?
mercy.hint: Efficiency is not the same as wisdom.
mercy.professor: Where is the person who cannot keep up?

final.title: The last word
final.prompt: {{topic}} Keep your answer, shrink it, or change it.
final.hint: A smaller true answer beats a huge fake one.
final.professor: Final answer. Would you still defend it if someone you love had to live under it?

claim.text: The mission matters more than the slow people.
claim.professor: That is your persona's strength turning into a blind spot.
claim.lesson: Every strength becomes dangerous when it stops loving people.

claim.text: My answer is: yes, but only with clear limits and real accountability.
claim.professor: Good. I can now see the claim well enough to test it.
claim.lesson: Clear claims can be checked.

claim.text: Bold action should serve people, not sacrifice them.
claim.professor: Good. You redeemed the strength instead of letting it become a monster.
claim.lesson: A gift becomes wisdom when it serves truth and people.

define.text: It means progress. You know, better stuff and better outcomes.
define.professor: That definition is wearing roller skates. Slow it down.
define.lesson: Vague words let bad arguments escape.

define.text: I mean practical success, not moral worth or final authority.
define.professor: Very good. You separated usefulness from value. Keep that distinction alive.
define.lesson: Useful is not the same as morally worthy.

define.text: I mean better in one limited area, not better at being human.
define.professor: Good. A tool can be better at a task without becoming better than a person.
define.lesson: Limited claims are often stronger claims.

assumption.text: I do not think there is a hidden assumption. The answer is just practical.
assumption.professor: Practical answers have assumptions too. They simply wear work boots.
assumption.lesson: Every practical answer still rests on beliefs.

assumption.text: I am assuming the system will be fair, accurate, and watched by responsible people.
assumption.professor: Good. Now we can test whether those conditions are real or imaginary.
assumption.lesson: Naming an assumption makes it testable.

assumption.text: I am assuming people will not abuse the power. That is the risky part.
assumption.professor: Excellent. You spotted the weak hinge in the door.
assumption.lesson: The biggest risk is often human misuse.

realLife.text: On paper, the system works well, so real life should follow.
realLife.professor: Paper is famously obedient. People are not paper.
realLife.lesson: Real life tests ideas harder than diagrams do.

realLife.text: Test it in a small setting first, watch for harm, and stop if people are being used.
realLife.professor: Good. You did not use humans as beta testers without brakes.
realLife.lesson: A good trial protects people while learning.

realLife.text: Start with the people closest to the impact and let them challenge the plan.
realLife.professor: Good. The affected people are not props. They get a voice.
realLife.lesson: The people affected should help test the idea.

humanCost.text: Some people will lose, but big progress always has casualties.
humanCost.professor: Calling people casualties is a fast way to lose the plot.
humanCost.lesson: Progress that treats people as disposable is not wisdom.

humanCost.text: The answer must protect the person with the least power, not only the winners.
humanCost.professor: Excellent. The weakest person is not a rounding error.
humanCost.lesson: Christian-shaped wisdom notices the vulnerable first.

humanCost.text: There may be trade-offs, but they must be named honestly and limited.
humanCost.professor: Good. You did not pretend the cost disappeared because the slide looked nice.
humanCost.lesson: Honest trade-offs are better than hidden harm.

power.text: Move fast and trust the builders. Delay is the real danger.
power.professor: Competence without limits becomes a throne very quickly.
power.lesson: Skill does not cancel the need for accountability.

power.text: Power needs limits, appeal, transparency, and a way to say no.
power.professor: Good. You remembered that power needs a fence.
power.lesson: Good systems limit power because people are fallible.

power.text: Use expertise, but keep final responsibility with accountable humans.
power.professor: Good. Experts can advise without becoming untouchable.
power.lesson: Advice is not the same as authority.

truth.text: I would change my mind if my side agreed I should.
truth.professor: That makes truth wait outside while the team votes.
truth.lesson: Truth cannot depend only on your group.

truth.text: I would change my mind if strong evidence showed real harm or a better explanation.
truth.professor: Excellent. A belief with a working door can still be corrected.
truth.lesson: Being correctable is strength, not weakness.

truth.text: I need the same standard of proof for my side and the other side.
truth.professor: Good. No special discount for your preferred answer.
truth.lesson: Use the same rule for both sides.

mercy.text: Mercy is nice, but the efficient answer should win.
mercy.professor: Efficiency is a fine servant and a terrible savior.
mercy.lesson: Mercy protects people from becoming numbers.

mercy.text: Mercy does not mean ignoring truth. It means refusing to erase people.
mercy.professor: Very good. Mercy is not mushy. It is strength with a human face.

mercy.text: The rule should leave room for the weak, the slow, and the person who failed.
mercy.professor: Good. A wise system makes room for people who are not optimized.

final.text: The mission matters more than the slow people.
final.professor: That is your persona's strength turning into a blind spot.
final.lesson: Every strength becomes dangerous when it stops loving people.

final.text: I would shrink my claim: this can help, but it should not rule people.
final.professor: Excellent. A smaller true answer beats a giant fake one.
final.lesson: Changing the size of a claim can make it wiser.

final.text: Bold action should serve people, not sacrifice them.
final.professor: Good. You redeemed the strength instead of letting it become a monster.
final.lesson: A gift becomes wisdom when it serves truth and people.
